question: Should `/v1/chat/completions` ever expose internal OpenClaw agent tool-call telemetry, or should `tool_calls` stay limited to caller-supplied HTTP client tools?
rationale: The current code and release docs define a client-tool contract, while exposing internal tool calls would change an operator-security boundary and likely require a new opt-in policy surface.

options.title: Keep the current client-tool contract
options.body: Treat internal tool-call telemetry as unsupported on this API, clarify docs if needed, and direct debugging to Gateway diagnostics or trajectory surfaces.

options.title: Design an opt-in diagnostic mode
options.body: Add a redacted, scoped, opt-in API or diagnostic surface for internal tool telemetry, with tests proving no default behavior or sensitive-data exposure changes.

options.title: Request a provider-specific repro first
options.body: Ask the reporter for a redacted qwen request/response and config so maintainers can decide whether this is actually a provider/tool-call parsing bug instead of an API contract request.

recommendation.title: Keep the current client-tool contract
recommendation.body: Treat internal tool-call telemetry as unsupported on this API, clarify docs if needed, and direct debugging to Gateway diagnostics or trajectory surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent adjacent Gateway tool-contract history and are the best available routing owner for the product/security boundary decision among the identified owners.
